{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p6-a1268138","text":"Textures are small (16x16). Let's understand:
- counter_side_drawer: drawer front (two drawers with handles) — that's the "front" of the drawer counter. 
- counter_stove_side: oven/stove side, off (black with flames? actually shows orange things), 
- counter_stove_side_on: stove on.
- counter_top: light grey countertop.
- counter_side: wood cabinet.
- counter_top_cutting: dark cutting board? looks dark square. Actually looks like a black/dark square, maybe it's a cutting board top.

User says: "Add Drawer counter block that functions like a Chest. ALSO; add the oven counter variant that functions exactly like a furnace. See git new files for the names of these textures."

So we need two blocks:
- "Drawer Counter" — functions like chest — uses counter_side_drawer texture for front (facing), counter_side for other sides, counter_top for top, spruce_planks for bottom. Like chest but counter.
- "Oven Counter" — functions exactly like furnace — uses counter_stove_side / counter_stove_side_on for front, counter_side for other sides, counter_top for top, spruce_planks bottom. Lit state.

Need to check:
1. How blocks get registered, hardcoded IDs. Need to pick free IDs (e.g., 314, 315? Check what IDs used up to 313). Let's find maximum IDs.
2. GuiContainerChest and GuiContainerFurnace require BlockEntity handling. Check World and BlockEntity and GuiContainerChest, GuiContainerFurnace to see if they're keyed by block type or generic "chest"/"furnace".
3. Server-side world (there may be an integrated worker / server with its own block definitions) - "offgridCommands.js" had counter, and "World.js", "WorldRenderer.js". Need to check server-side block registry perhaps src/js/net/minecraft/server/... maybe this is a singleplayer integrated server. Let's search for "furnace" and "chest" references.
4. Textures loading: assetManifest.js probably includes texture names. Let's check.
5. Block breaking drops/picked item.
6. Crafting recipes? The task says add block that functions like chest/furnace; likely need creative inventory tab, maybe crafting recipes are defined elsewhere. Let's look.

            if (!item || item.isEmpty()) {
                return { typeId: 0, count: 0 };
            }
            return { typeId: item.getType(), count: item.getCount() };
        };

        return {
            size: this.items.length,
            items: this.items.map(serializeItem)
        };

            return;

        const size = Number(state.size || items.length || 0);
        this.items = new Array(size).fill(null).map((_, index) => {
            const slot = items[index];
            return new ItemStack(slot?.typeId || 0, slot?.count || 0);
        });

        for (const key of Object.keys(state)) {
            if (key !== 'size' && key !== 'items') {
                this[key] = state[key];
            }
        }

 * Resolve a renderer-supplied path to an absolute path inside MODS_DIR.
 * Throws on traversal attempts, NUL bytes, absolute paths and anything

function resolveModPath(relPath) {
    if (typeof relPath !== 'string') {
        throw new Error('Invalid path');
    }
    // An empty path addresses the mods root itself, not an invalid request:
    // listDir('') is the documented way to ask for the whole folder (see the
    // preload bridge), and BridgeFilesystem opens its index with exactly that
    // call. Rejecting it made every mod lookup fail in the packaged build,
    // where the renderer reaches the disk through this bridge. It stays inside
    // the sandbox - '' normalises to no segments, so it resolves to MODS_DIR and
    // still passes the containment check at the end of this function.
    if (relPath.includes('\0')) {
        throw new Error('Invalid path');
    }

    // Normalise separators and strip './' or leading slashes so that
    // 'mods/a/b', '/mods/a/b' and './mods/a/b' all mean the same thing.
    let normalized = relPath.replace(/\\/g, '/').replace(/^\.?\//, '');

    // Collapse '.' segments and reject '..' outright rather than trying to
    // resolve them - a mods file never legitimately needs to go up.
    const segments = normalized.split('/').filter((s) => s !== '' && s !== '.');
    if (segments.some((s) => s === '..')) {
        throw new Error('Path traversal is not allowed');
    }

    // The renderer addresses files by their virtual path, which is rooted
    // at 'mods/' (e.g. 'mods/my_mod/ModData.json'). MODS_DIR already *is*
    // that folder, so drop the leading segment when present. Accepting a
    // bare 'my_mod/...' too keeps the handler usable on its own.
    if (segments[0] === 'mods') {
        segments.shift();
    }

    const abs = path.resolve(MODS_DIR, ...segments);
    const rootWithSep = MODS_DIR.endsWith(path.sep) ? MODS_DIR : MODS_DIR + path.sep;
    if (abs !== MODS_DIR && !abs.startsWith(rootWithSep)) {
        throw new Error('Path escapes the mods directory');
    }
    return abs;
}

import Block from "../Block.js";
import BlockChest from "./BlockChest.js";
import BoundingBox from "../../../../util/BoundingBox.js";
import EnumBlockFace from "../../../../util/EnumBlockFace.js";
import EnumCreativeInventoryTab from "../../../gui/EnumCreativeInventoryTab.js";

export default class BlockCounterDrawer extends BlockChest {

    constructor(id, textureSlotId) {
        super(id, textureSlotId);
        this.description = "Drawer Counter";
        this.hardness = 2.0;
        this.sound = Block.sounds.wood;
        this.boundingBox = new BoundingBox(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0);
        this.noFaceCull = false;
        this.inventoryTab = EnumCreativeInventoryTab.MACHINES;
    }

    shouldRenderFace(world, x, y, z, face, prefetchedTypeId) {
        return Block.prototype.shouldRenderFace.call(this, world, x, y, z, face, prefetchedTypeId);
    }

    getAmbientOcclusion() {
        return true;
    }

    getTextureForFace(face, data) {
        let facing = data & 7;
        if (facing === 0) facing = 2;
        const frontTex = 'counter_side_drawer';
        switch (face) {
            case EnumBlockFace.NORTH:
                return facing === 2 ? frontTex : 'counter_side';
            case EnumBlockFace.SOUTH:
                return facing === 3 ? frontTex : 'counter_side';
            case EnumBlockFace.WEST:
                return facing === 4 ? frontTex : 'counter_side';
            case EnumBlockFace.EAST:
                return facing === 5 ? frontTex : 'counter_side';
            case EnumBlockFace.TOP:
                return 'counter_top';
            case EnumBlockFace.BOTTOM:
                return 'spruce_planks';
            default:
                return 'counter_side';
        }
    }

    getContainerTitle() {
        return "Drawer Counter";
    }
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"k6VUzG75BQg","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/js/net/minecraft/client/render/model/ObjModel.js","instructions":"Add a minimal OBJ model parser for rendering custom block models.","content":"/**
 * Minimal Wavefront OBJ parser for static block models.
 *
 * Supports the subset Blockbench exports for custom block models: vertex,
 * texture-coordinate and face records. Polygons are triangulated so callers can
 * emit every triangle through the block Tessellator.
 */
export default class ObjModel {

    constructor(faces) {
        this.faces = faces;
    }

    static parse(text) {
        const positions = [];
        const textureCoords = [];
        const faces = [];

        for (const rawLine of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
            const line = rawLine.trim();
            if (!line || line.startsWith('#')) {
                continue;
            }

            const parts = line.split(/\s+/);
            switch (parts[0]) {
                case 'v':
                    positions.push([
                        Number(parts[1]) || 0,
                        Number(parts[2]) || 0,
                        Number(parts[3]) || 0
                    ]);
                    break;

                case 'vt':
                    textureCoords.push([
                        Number(parts[1]) || 0,
                        Number(parts[2]) || 0
                    ]);
                    break;

                case 'f': {
                    const vertices = [];
                    for (let i = 1; i < parts.length; i++) {
                        const indices = parts[i].split('/');
                        const positionIndex = ObjModel.resolveIndex(indices[0], positions.length);
                        if (positionIndex === null) {
                            continue;
                        }

                        const uvIndex = indices.length > 1
                            ? ObjModel.resolveIndex(indices[1], textureCoords.length)
                            : null;

                        vertices.push({
                            position: positions[positionIndex],
                            uv: uvIndex === null ? [0, 0] : textureCoords[uvIndex]
                        });
                    }

                    // Fan triangulation. Faces exported by Blockbench are
                    // triangles or quads, but this keeps arbitrary polygons safe.
                    for (let i = 1; i < vertices.length - 1; i++) {
                        faces.push(ObjModel.createTriangle(vertices[0], vertices[i], vertices[i + 1]));
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        return new ObjModel(faces);
    }

    static resolveIndex(token, length) {
        const raw = Number.parseInt(token, 10);
        if (!Number.isFinite(raw)) {
            return null;
        }

        const index = raw < 0 ? length + raw : raw - 1;
        return index >= 0 && index < length ? index : null;
    }

    static createTriangle(a, b, c) {
        const abx = b.position[0] - a.position[0];
        const aby = b.position[1] - a.position[1];
        const abz = b.position[2] - a.position[2];
        const acx = c.position[0] - a.position[0];
        const acy = c.position[1] - a.position[1];
        const acz = c.position[2] - a.position[2];

        let nx = aby * acz - abz * acy;
        let ny = abz * acx - abx * acz;
        let nz = abx * acy - aby * acx;
        const length = Math.hypot(nx, ny, nz) || 1;
        nx /= length;
        ny /= length;
        nz /= length;

        return {
            vertices: [a, b, c],
            normal: [nx, ny, nz]
        };
    }
}

    const comma = dataUri.indexOf(",");

        return "";
    }
    return atob(dataUri.slice(comma + 1));
}

/**

 * embedded by scripts/build-assets.js, so it also works in the single-file
 * build where runtime file requests are unavailable.
 */
export default function getTrafficConeModel() {
    if (parsedModel !== undefined) {
        return parsedModel;
    }

    const asset = base64Assets[MODEL_ASSET];
    if (!asset) {
        console.warn(`[TrafficCone] Missing bundled model asset: ${MODEL_ASSET}`);

export default class GiveCommand extends Command {

    constructor() {
        super("give", "<item> [count]", "Give yourself an item")
    }

    execute(minecraft, args) {
        if (args.length < 1) {
            return false;
        }

        let itemName = args[0].toLowerCase();
        let count = 1;
        if (args.length >= 2) {
            count = parseInt(args[1]);
            if (isNaN(count) || count <= 0) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        let block = BlockRegistry.get(itemName);
        if (!block) {
            minecraft.addMessageToChat("Item not found: " + args[0]);
            return true;
        }

        let player = minecraft.player;
        if (!player) {
            minecraft.addMessageToChat("No player available");
            return true;
        }

        let added = player.inventory.addItem(block.id, count);
        if (added) {
            minecraft.addMessageToChat("Gave " + count + " x " + itemName);
        } else {
            minecraft.addMessageToChat("Inventory full!");
        }

        return true;
    }

}

+export default class BlockTrafficCone extends Block {
+
+    constructor(id, textureSlotId) {
+        super(id, textureSlotId);
+        this.description = "Traffic Cone";
+        this.hardness = 0.3;
+        this.sound = Block.sounds.cloth;
+        this.inventoryTab = EnumCreativeInventoryTab.DECORATION;

+    }

+

import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import {
    uiTextures,
    atlasBlockTextures,
    atlasItemTextures,
    atlasPaintingTextures,
    modelAssets,
    musicTracks,
    soundPools,
    clickSound,
} from '../src/js/assetManifest.js';

const RESOURCES_DIR = path.resolve('src/resources');
const OUTPUT_FILE = path.resolve('src/resources.js');

// Music is chunked and fetched lazily by MusicManager (URL fallback), so it is
// excluded from the base64 bundle by default. Pass --include-music to embed it
// (used by the offline single-file build).
const includeMusic = process.argv.includes('--include-music');

const MIME_TYPES = {
    '.png': 'image/png',
    '.jpg': 'image/jpeg',
    '.jpeg': 'image/jpeg',
    '.gif': 'image/gif',
    '.webp': 'image/webp',
    '.ogg': 'audio/ogg',
    '.mp3': 'audio/mpeg',
    '.obj': 'text/plain'
};

// Every asset the game actually uses, keyed the same way as base64Assets
// (relative to src/resources/). Only these files get embedded.
const wantedKeys = new Set([...uiTextures, clickSound]);
// Keys that must exist on disk (sound pool variants are optional - the game
// gracefully falls back when numbered/unnumbered variants are absent).
const criticalKeys = new Set([...uiTextures, clickSound]);

if (includeMusic) {
    for (const track of Object.values(musicTracks).flat()) {
        wantedKeys.add(track);
        criticalKeys.add(track);
    }
}

for (const pool of soundPools) {
    const rel = pool.replace('.', '/');
    for (let i = 1; i <= 6; i++) {
        wantedKeys.add(`sound/${rel}${i}.ogg`);
    }
    wantedKeys.add(`sound/${rel}.ogg`);
}

for (const name of atlasBlockTextures) {
    wantedKeys.add(`terrain/pack/minecraft/textures/blocks/${name}`);
    criticalKeys.add(`terrain/pack/minecraft/textures/blocks/${name}`);
}
for (const name of atlasItemTextures) {
    wantedKeys.add(`terrain/pack/minecraft/textures/items/${name}`);
    criticalKeys.add(`terrain/pack/minecraft/textures/items/${name}`);
}
for (const name of atlasPaintingTextures) {
    wantedKeys.add(`terrain/pack/minecraft/textures/painting/${name}`);
    criticalKeys.add(`terrain/pack/minecraft/textures/painting/${name}`);
}
for (const model of modelAssets) {
    wantedKeys.add(model);
    criticalKeys.add(model);
}

function walkDir(dir, fileList = []) {
    const files = fs.readdirSync(dir);
    for (const file of files) {
        const filePath = path.join(dir, file);
        if (fs.statSync(filePath).isDirectory()) {
            walkDir(filePath, fileList);
        } else {
            fileList.push(filePath);
        }
    }
    return fileList;
}

const allFiles = walkDir(RESOURCES_DIR);
const availableKeys = new Set();
const assetMap = {};
const hashToKey = {};
const aliases = [];
let dedupedCount = 0;
let dedupedBytes = 0;
let skippedCount = 0;
let skippedBytes = 0;

for (const filePath of allFiles) {
    const ext = path.extname(filePath).toLowerCase();
    if (!MIME_TYPES[ext]) continue;

    // Relativize path to match the game's texture keys (e.g., "gui/font.png")
    const relativePath = path.relative(RESOURCES_DIR, filePath).replace(/\\/g, '/');

    // Only bundle assets the game actually uses (see src/js/assetManifest.js)
    if (!wantedKeys.has(relativePath)) {
        skippedCount++;
        skippedBytes += fs.statSync(filePath).size;
        continue;
    }
    availableKeys.add(relativePath);

    const fileBuffer = fs.readFileSync(filePath);

    // Deduplicate identical file contents: store the base64 once and
    // alias every duplicate key to the first occurrence. Identical files
    // are common (texture packs mirror the vanilla sound/music trees).
    const contentHash = crypto.createHash('md5').update(fileBuffer).digest('hex');
    const firstKey = hashToKey[contentHash];
    if (firstKey) {
        aliases.push([relativePath, firstKey]);
        dedupedCount++;
        dedupedBytes += fileBuffer.length;
        continue;
    }
    hashToKey[contentHash] = relativePath;

    const base64 = fileBuffer.toString('base64');
    assetMap[relativePath] = `data:${MIME_TYPES[ext]};base64,${base64}`;
}

// Warn about critical manifest entries that have no file on disk, so list
// drift is visible. (Optional sound pool variants are skipped silently.)
const missingKeys = [...criticalKeys].filter(key => !availableKeys.has(key));
for (const key of missingKeys) {
    console.warn(`[build-assets] Manifest lists asset not found on disk, skipping: ${key}`);
}

const aliasLines = aliases.map(([alias, target]) =>
    `base64Assets[${JSON.stringify(alias)}] = base64Assets[${JSON.stringify(target)}];`
);

const fileContent =
    `// Auto-generated Base64 assets\n` +
    `// Only assets listed in src/js/assetManifest.js are bundled.\n` +
    `// Deduplicated: ${dedupedCount} assets share the same content and reference an existing copy.\n` +
    `export const base64Assets = ${JSON.stringify(assetMap, null, 2)};\n` +
    `\n` +
    aliasLines.join('\n') +
    `\n`;

fs.writeFileSync(OUTPUT_FILE, fileContent);

const totalKeys = Object.keys(assetMap).length + aliases.length;
const outSize = fs.statSync(OUTPUT_FILE).size;
const inSize = allFiles.reduce((sum, f) => {
    return sum + (wantedKeys.has(path.relative(RESOURCES_DIR, f).replace(/\\/g, '/')) ? fs.statSync(f).size : 0);
}, 0);
console.log(`Converted ${totalKeys} of ${wantedKeys.size} wanted assets to Base64 in src/resources.js`);
if (!includeMusic) {
    console.log('Music tracks excluded from bundle (lazy-loaded by URL). Use --include-music to embed them.');
}
console.log(`Skipped ${skippedCount} unused assets (saved ${(skippedBytes / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB raw)`);
console.log(`Embedded ${(inSize / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB raw -> ${(outSize / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB base64 in src/resources.js`);
console.log(`Deduplicated ${dedupedCount} identical files (saved ${(dedupedBytes / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB raw / ~${(dedupedBytes * 1.333 / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB base64)`);

Progress note:
Added folder-based mod installation alongside ZIPs.

**What changed**

- [ModLoader.js](src/js/net/minecraft/client/ModLoader.js) now has `installModFromFolder(fileList)`.
  - Accepts the `FileList` produced by a directory picker.
  - Finds `ModData.js` or `ModData.json` and automatically strips the selected folder prefix.
  - Rejects selections containing multiple mod roots.
  - Copies the full folder into the normal persistent mod layout: scripts, blocks, items, commands, GUI files, textures, sounds, helpers, and `ModData.js`.
  - Converts PNG/OGG/JPG/WAV/etc. files into the loader’s expected `<name>.b64` format.
  - Writes a normalized `ModData.json`, enables the mod, and loads it immediately.
- [GuiMods.js](src/js/net/minecraft/client/gui/screens/GuiMods.js) has a new **Upload folder** button in the top-right. It opens a directory chooser via `webkitdirectory`, then refreshes the mod list and selects the new mod.
- Added the `Upload folder` translation for Spanish and Hungarian.

The existing physical `mods/` folder loading is unchanged; this adds folder installation through the UI as well.

`npx vite build` and `git diff --check` pass, and `node --check` passes for both edited source files. I also ran the folder installer against a fake `FileList` containing `ModData.js`, `ModLoad.js`, a block, a texture, and a sound; all files landed in the expected persistent paths and the mod was enabled and loaded. Implemented the fix.

The singleplayer world runs in a separate worker, and that worker previously only looked for mods in the world’s `servermods/` folder. A mod installed from the client’s Mods screen (or the physical `mods/` folder) was therefore never registered server-side, so `/plot` fell through to the “only installed on your client” message.

What changed:

- [ModLoader.js](src/js/net/minecraft/client/ModLoader.js) now builds a server-compatible snapshot of every locally loaded mod, including its scripts and assets. Mods received from a remote server are excluded.
- [Minecraft.js](src/js/net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.js) passes that snapshot when starting the integrated server for both new and saved worlds.
- [integrated.worker.js](src/js/net/minecraft/client/integrated/integrated.worker.js) hands the snapshot to the server-mod loader before the world initializes, and clears it when the world stops.
- [serverMods.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/serverMods.js) merges those in-memory mods with the world’s existing `servermods/` directory. A real folder in `servermods/` still takes priority for the same mod ID.

With this, the Plots mod’s `ModLoad.js` runs in the integrated server, registers `/plot`, and its block-protection hooks become authoritative in singleplayer. Nothing is copied into the save, so uninstalling or disabling the mod takes effect the next time the world loads.

`npx vite build` completed successfully. I did not launch a live world to click through `/plot`.

Progress note:
Added `SERVER_MOD_URLS` for standalone server startup.

Usage:

```sh
SERVER_MOD_URLS="https://mods.breakmine.com/view/10,https://mods.breakmine.com/view/12" node server.js
```

Behavior:

- Accepts `/view/<id>` pages, direct `/download/...` links, and `.zip` URLs.
- Resolves view pages to their newest `/download/<id>/v/<version>` archive, so `view/10` installs `download/10/v/18` automatically.
- Supports comma-, semicolon-, or whitespace-separated lists.
- Installs into the active server’s `servermods/` directory before mods are loaded, so downloaded mods are registered and sent to joining players through the normal server-mod flow.
- Replaces previously URL-installed copies on restart, using a `.from-wiki` marker.
- Rejects oversized archives, caps requests at 30 seconds, extracts without allowing path traversal, and logs failures without preventing server startup.

Files changed:

- [serverModDownloads.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/serverModDownloads.js) — downloader/resolver/extractor.
- [server.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/server.js) — runs the installer before `initServer()`.
- [README.md](README.md) — usage docs.

import PacketHandler from "./PacketHandler.js";
import EncryptionResponsePacket from "../packet/login/client/EncryptionResponsePacket.js";
import CryptManager from "../util/CryptManager.js";
import GuiDisconnected from "../../gui/screens/GuiDisconnected.js";
import Authentication from "../util/Authentication.js";
import NetworkPlayHandler from "./NetworkPlayHandler.js";
import ProtocolState from "../ProtocolState.js";

export default class NetworkLoginHandler extends PacketHandler {

    constructor(networkManager) {
        super();

        this.networkManager = networkManager;
        this.authentication = new Authentication(networkManager);
    }

    handleEncryptionRequest(packet) {
        // Create an AES key for the packet encryption
        let secretKey = CryptManager.createNewSharedKey();

        // Send join server request to Mojang
        let session = this.networkManager.minecraft.getSession();
        let serverId = this.authentication.createServerHash(packet.serverId, secretKey, packet.publicKey);
        this.authentication.joinServer(session.getProfile(), session.getAccessToken(), serverId);

        // Send encryption response
        this.networkManager.sendPacket(new EncryptionResponsePacket(secretKey, packet.publicKey, packet.verifyToken));

        // Enable encryption
        this.networkManager.enableEncryption(secretKey);
    }

    handleLoginDisconnect(packet) {
        this.disconnectReason = packet.message;
        console.log("[Network] Disconnected from server: " + this.disconnectReason);
        this.networkManager.minecraft.displayScreen(new GuiDisconnected(this.disconnectReason));
    }

    handleLoginSuccess(packet) {
        this.networkManager.setState(ProtocolState.PLAY);
        this.networkManager.setNetworkHandler(new NetworkPlayHandler(this.networkManager, packet.profile));
    }

    handleEnableCompression(packet) {
        this.networkManager.setCompressionThreshold(packet.getCompressionThreshold());
    }

    onDisconnect() {
        if (this.networkManager.minecraft.isInGame()) {
            this.networkManager.minecraft.displayScreen(new GuiDisconnected(this.disconnectReason || "Disconnected from server"));
        }
    }

{"kind":"tool","id":"l5nN-Giw_-k","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/js/net/minecraft/server/security.js","content":"// Connection hardening for the standalone multiplayer server.
//
// Two independent layers live here:
//
//   1. Anti-DDoS: refuse floods of new sockets from one address, cap the
//      number of sockets an address may hold open, and rate-limit the messages
//      an established socket can send. Repeat offenders are blocked for a
//      while instead of being hammered on individually.
//
//   2. Anti-VPN: ask an IP-reputation service whether an address belongs to a
//      VPN, proxy or hosting provider and refuse the login when it does.
//      Results are cached (reputation changes slowly), lookups never block the
//      event loop, and a service outage falls back to the configured
//      fail-open/fail-closed behaviour.
//
// Everything in here is inert unless the server is running under Node and a
// real socket request is available, so the singleplayer integrated server
// (which runs inside a browser worker and is reached through a loopback
// adapter) is never affected.
import { createDisconnectPacket } from './packets.js';
import Logger from './logger.js';

const log = Logger;

const ENV = (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env) || {};
const IS_NODE = typeof process !== 'undefined' && !!(process.versions && process.versions.node);

function envFlag(name, fallback) {
    const raw = ENV[name];
    if (typeof raw !== 'string' || raw.trim() === '') return fallback;
    const value = raw.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (['0', 'false', 'no', 'off'].includes(value)) return false;
    if (['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes(value)) return true;
    return fallback;
}

function envInt(name, fallback, min, max) {
    const parsed = parseInt(ENV[name], 10);
    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;
    return Math.max(min, Math.min(max, parsed));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Settings
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const settings = {
    antiDdos: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIDDOS', true),
    antiVpn: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIVPN', true),
    // "ipapi" needs no account (free, non-commercial, HTTP only). "proxycheck"
    // is more accurate and adds datacenter detection, but needs a key.
    vpnProvider: String(ENV.SERVER_ANTIVPN_PROVIDER || 'ipapi').trim().toLowerCase(),
    vpnKey: String(ENV.SERVER_ANTIVPN_KEY || '').trim(),
    // Datacenter/hosting ranges are blocked by default: a server owner who only
    // wants to stop VPNs (and not, say, cloud-hosted friends) can turn this off.
    blockHosting: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIVPN_BLOCK_HOSTING', true),
    // Fail open keeps the server playable when the reputation service is down.
    vpnFailOpen: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIVPN_FAIL_OPEN', true),
    vpnTimeoutMs: envInt('SERVER_ANTIVPN_TIMEOUT_MS', 3000, 250, 15000),
    // Only enable when the server sits behind a reverse proxy that overwrites
    // X-Forwarded-For; otherwise clients could spoof their address.
    trustProxy: envFlag('SERVER_TRUST_PROXY', false)
};

// Flood limits. Generous enough for normal play (a client sends ~20 position
// updates a second) but orders of magnitude below what a spray attack needs.
const CONNECTION_WINDOW_MS = 10 * 1000;
const MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_WINDOW = 12;
const MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_IP = 5;
const MAX_TOTAL_CONNECTIONS = 256;
const MESSAGE_BURST = 900;
const MESSAGE_REFILL_PER_SECOND = 300;
const MAX_TEXT_MESSAGE_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_BINARY_MESSAGE_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024;

const VIOLATION_WINDOW_MS = 30 * 1000;
const VIOLATION_LIMIT = 12;
const BAN_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;

const VPN_CACHE_TTL_MS = 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const VPN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 5000;
// How many login/movement messages are replayed once a pending VPN verdict
// arrives. A client only sends a handful before it is in game.
const MAX_HELD_MESSAGES = 32;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// State
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const bans = new Map(); // ip -> expiresAt
const connectionHistory = new Map(); // ip -> { count, windowStart }
const activeConnections = new Map(); // ip -> open socket count
const violations = new Map(); // ip -> { score, since }
const vpnCache = new Map(); // ip -> { blocked, reason, expires }
let totalConnections = 0;
let warnedNoKey = false;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Addressing helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function normalizeAddress(ip) {
    if (!ip) return null;
    let address = String(ip).trim();
    if (!address) return null;
    // IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:1.2.3.4) and zone ids must not split the cache.
    if (address.startsWith('::ffff:') && address.includes('.')) {
        address = address.slice(7);
    }
    const zone = address.indexOf('%');
    if (zone !== -1) address = address.slice(0, zone);
    return address || null;
}

export function getClientIp(req) {
    if (!req) return null;

    if (settings.trustProxy && req.headers) {
        const forwarded = req.headers['x-forwarded-for'];
        if (typeof forwarded === 'string' && forwarded.trim()) {
            return normalizeAddress(forwarded.split(',')[0]);
        }
    }

    const socket = req.socket || req.connection;
    return normalizeAddress(socket && socket.remoteAddress);
}

// Loopback, LAN and CGNAT addresses are never looked up: they are not public
// VPN endpoints, and looking them up only burns the provider's rate limit.
function isLocalAddress(ip) {
    if (!ip) return true;
    if (ip === '::1' || ip === '0.0.0.0' || ip === '::') return true;
    if (/^127\./.test(ip)) return true;
    if (/^10\./.test(ip)) return true;
    if (/^192\.168\./.test(ip)) return true;
    if (/^172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\./.test(ip)) return true;
    if (/^169\.254\./.test(ip)) return true;
    if (/^100\.(6[4-9]|[7-9]\d|1[01]\d|12[0-7])\./.test(ip)) return true;
    const lower = ip.toLowerCase();
    if (lower.startsWith('fc') || lower.startsWith('fd')) return true; // IPv6 ULA
    if (lower.startsWith('fe80:')) return true; // IPv6 link-local
    return false;
}

function isBanned(ip, now) {
    const until = bans.get(ip);
    if (!until) return false;
    if (until > now) return true;
    bans.delete(ip);
    return false;
}

function ban(ip, reason) {
    bans.set(ip, Date.now() + BAN_MS);
    log.warn('Security', `Temporarily blocked ${ip} for ${Math.round(BAN_MS / 60000)} min (${reason})`);
}

function countViolation(ip, reason) {
    const now = Date.now();
    let record = violations.get(ip);
    if (!record || now - record.since > VIOLATION_WINDOW_MS) {
        record = { score: 0, since: now };
        violations.set(ip, record);
    }
    record.score += 1;
    if (record.score >= VIOLATION_LIMIT) {
        violations.delete(ip);
        ban(ip, reason);
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}

function releaseConnection(ip) {
    const open = (activeConnections.get(ip) || 1) - 1;
    if (open <= 0) activeConnections.delete(ip);
    else activeConnections.set(ip, open);
    totalConnections = Math.max(0, totalConnections - 1);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Admission control (ws `verifyClient`): runs before the HTTP upgrade
// completes, so refused clients never get a WebSocket.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Decide whether a new upgrade may open a socket.
 *
 * @returns {{accepted: boolean, ip?: string, code?: number, message?: string, reason?: string}}
 */
export function verifyConnection(info) {
    if (!IS_NODE || !settings.antiDdos) {
        return { accepted: true };
    }

    const req = info && info.req;
    const ip = getClientIp(req);
    if (!ip) {
        return { accepted: true };
    }

    const now = Date.now();

    if (isBanned(ip, now)) {
        return {
            accepted: false,
            ip,
            code: 403,
            message: 'Your address is temporarily blocked.',
            reason: 'address is temporarily blocked'
        };
    }

    if (totalConnections >= MAX_TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) {
        return {
            accepted: false,
            ip,
            code: 503,
            message: 'Server is full, try again later.',
            reason: `total connection cap (${MAX_TOTAL_CONNECTIONS}) reached`
        };
    }

    const open = activeConnections.get(ip) || 0;
    if (open >= MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_IP) {
        countViolation(ip, 'too many concurrent sockets');
        return {
            accepted: false,
            ip,
            code: 429,
            message: 'Too many connections from your address.',
            reason: `${open} sockets already open`
        };
    }

    let history = connectionHistory.get(ip);
    if (!history || now - history.windowStart > CONNECTION_WINDOW_MS) {
        history = { count: 0, windowStart: now };
        connectionHistory.set(ip, history);
    }
    history.count += 1;
    if (history.count > MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_WINDOW) {
        const banned = countViolation(ip, 'connection flood');
        return {
            accepted: false,
            ip,
            code: 429,
            message: 'Too many connection attempts, slow down.',
            reason: banned
                ? `connection flood (${history.count} attempts in ${CONNECTION_WINDOW_MS / 1000}s), banned`
                : `connection flood (${history.count} attempts in ${CONNECTION_WINDOW_MS / 1000}s)`
        };
    }

    activeConnections.set(ip, open + 1);
    totalConnections += 1;

    // The socket may close before (or without) the WebSocket handshake
    // finishing, so release the slot from the socket itself.
    const socket = req && (req.socket || req.connection);
    if (socket && typeof socket.once === 'function') {
        socket.once('close', () => releaseConnection(ip));
    }

    return { accepted: true, ip };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Anti-VPN lookups
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function readVpnCache(ip, now) {
    const entry = vpnCache.get(ip);
    if (!entry) return null;
    if (entry.expires <= now) {
        vpnCache.delete(ip);
        return null;
    }
    return entry;
}

function writeVpnCache(ip, blocked, reason) {
    if (vpnCache.size >= VPN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES) {
        // Map keeps insertion order: drop the oldest verdict.
        const oldest = vpnCache.keys().next();
        if (!oldest.done) vpnCache.delete(oldest.value);
    }
    vpnCache.set(ip, { blocked, reason, expires: Date.now() + VPN_CACHE_TTL_MS });
}

async function fetchJson(url) {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), settings.vpnTimeoutMs);
    try {
        const response = await fetch(url, {
            signal: controller.signal,
            headers: { accept: 'application/json' }
        });
        if (!response.ok) {
            throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
        }
        return await response.json();
    } finally {
        clearTimeout(timer);
    }
}

async function lookupIpApi(ip) {
    const data = await fetchJson(
        `http://ip-api.com/json/${encodeURIComponent(ip)}?fields=status,message,proxy,hosting,countryCode`
    );
    if (!data || data.status !== 'success') {
        throw new Error((data && data.message) || 'lookup failed');
    }
    if (data.proxy === true) {
        return { blocked: true, reason: 'VPN or proxy' };
    }
    if (settings.blockHosting && data.hosting === true) {
        return { blocked: true, reason: 'datacenter/hosting address' };
    }
    return { blocked: false, reason: '' };
}

async function lookupProxycheck(ip) {
    const data = await fetchJson(
        `https://proxycheck.io/v2/${encodeURIComponent(ip)}?key=${encodeURIComponent(settings.vpnKey)}&vpn=1&asn=1`
    );
    if (!data || (data.status !== 'ok' && data.status !== 'warning')) {
        throw new Error((data && data.message) || 'lookup failed');
    }
    const entry = data[ip] || {};
    if (String(entry.proxy).toLowerCase() === 'yes') {
        const type = String(entry.type || 'VPN').trim();
        return { blocked: true, reason: `${type.toLowerCase()} address` };
    }
    if (settings.blockHosting && /hosting|datacenter|server/i.test(String(entry.type || ''))) {
        return { blocked: true, reason: 'datacenter/hosting address' };
    }
    return { blocked: false, reason: '' };
}

async function lookupVpn(ip) {
    const wantsProxycheck = settings.vpnProvider === 'proxycheck' || settings.vpnProvider === 'proxycheck.io';
    if (wantsProxycheck) {
        if (settings.vpnKey) {
            return lookupProxycheck(ip);
        }
        if (!warnedNoKey) {
            warnedNoKey = true;
            log.warn('Security', 'SERVER_ANTIVPN_PROVIDER=proxycheck needs SERVER_ANTIVPN_KEY; falling back to ip-api.com');
        }
    }
    return lookupIpApi(ip);
}

/**
 * Resolve whether an address may join. Never throws: a failed lookup resolves
 * to the configured fail-open/fail-closed verdict.
 */
export function checkAddress(ip) {
    const address = normalizeAddress(ip);
    if (!address || !settings.antiVpn || isLocalAddress(address)) {
        return Promise.resolve({ blocked: false, reason: '', skipped: true });
    }

    const cached = readVpnCache(address, Date.now());
    if (cached) {
        return Promise.resolve({ blocked: cached.blocked, reason: cached.reason });

function messageSize(message) {
    if (typeof message === 'string') return message.length;
    if (message && typeof message.byteLength === 'number') return message.byteLength;
    if (message && typeof message.length === 'number') return message.length;
    return 0;

/**
 * Build the per-socket gate. Returns null when there is no real socket (the
 * integrated singleplayer server) or when both protections are disabled.
 */
export function createConnectionGate(req, ws) {
    if (!IS_NODE || !req || (!settings.antiDdos && !settings.antiVpn)) {
        return null;
    }

    const ip = getClientIp(req);
    if (!ip) return null;

    const gate = {
        ip,
        // Called by the caller for each message released after a pending VPN
        // verdict, so buffered messages re-enter the normal handler.
        onFlush: null,
        held: [],
        tokens: MESSAGE_BURST,
        lastRefill: Date.now(),
        closed: false,
        denied: false,
        vpnPending: settings.antiVpn && !isLocalAddress(ip),
        vpnAllowed: !settings.antiVpn || isLocalAddress(ip),
        ws
    };

    function closeSocket() {
        if (gate.closed) return;
        gate.closed = true;
        try {
            if (ws && ws.readyState === 1) ws.close();
        } catch (e) {
            // Closing an already-broken socket is not an error.
        }
    }

    function deny(reason) {
        gate.denied = true;
        gate.held.length = 0;
        try {
            if (ws && ws.readyState === 1) {
                ws.send(createDisconnectPacket(`§c${reason}`));
            }
        } catch (e) {
            // Fall through to the close below.
        }
        log.info('Security', `Refused ${ip}: ${reason}`);
        closeSocket();
    }

    function refillTokens() {
        const now = Date.now();
        const elapsed = (now - gate.lastRefill) / 1000;
        if (elapsed <= 0) return;
        gate.lastRefill = now;
        gate.tokens = Math.min(
            MESSAGE_BURST,
            gate.tokens + elapsed * MESSAGE_REFILL_PER_SECOND
        );
    }

    gate.beforeMessage = function beforeMessage(message, isBinary) {
        if (gate.closed) return 'drop';

        if (settings.antiDdos) {
            const limit = isBinary ? MAX_BINARY_MESSAGE_BYTES : MAX_TEXT_MESSAGE_BYTES;
            if (messageSize(message) > limit) {
                countViolation(ip, 'oversized message');
                closeSocket();
                return 'drop';
            }

            refillTokens();
            if (gate.tokens < 1) {
                const banned = countViolation(ip, 'message flood');
                if (banned) {
                    closeSocket();
                }
                return 'drop';
            }
            gate.tokens -= 1;
        }

        if (gate.denied) return 'drop';

        if (gate.vpnPending) {
            if (gate.held.length < MAX_HELD_MESSAGES) {
                gate.held.push({ message, isBinary });
            }
            return 'hold';
        }

        return gate.vpnAllowed ? 'ok' : 'drop';
    };

    gate.dispose = function dispose() {
        gate.closed = true;
        gate.held.length = 0;
    };

    if (gate.vpnPending) {
        checkAddress(ip)
            .then((verdict) => {
                if (gate.closed) return;
                gate.vpnPending = false;
                if (verdict.blocked) {
                    deny(`Connections through ${verdict.reason || 'a VPN or proxy'} are not allowed on this server.`);
                    return;
                }
                gate.vpnAllowed = true;
                const queued = gate.held.splice(0);
                if (typeof gate.onFlush === 'function') {
                    for (const entry of queued) {
                        gate.onFlush(entry.message, entry.isBinary);
                    }
                }
            })
            .catch((error) => {
                gate.vpnPending = false;
                gate.vpnAllowed = true;
                log.warn('Security', `VPN gate for ${ip} failed open: ${error.message}`);
                const queued = gate.held.splice(0);
                if (typeof gate.onFlush === 'function') {
                    for (const entry of queued) {
                        gate.onFlush(entry.message, entry.isBinary);
                    }
                }
            });
    }

    return gate;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Maintenance + startup summary
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function sweep() {
    const now = Date.now();

    for (const [ip, until] of bans) {
        if (until <= now) bans.delete(ip);

    for (const [ip, record] of violations) {
        if (now - record.since > VIOLATION_WINDOW_MS) violations.delete(ip);

        if (now - history.windowStart > CONNECTION_WINDOW_MS && !activeConnections.has(ip)) {

    }

        if (entry.expires <= now) vpnCache.delete(ip);
    }
}

if (IS_NODE) {
    const timer = setInterval(sweep, 60 * 1000);
    if (typeof timer.unref === 'function') timer.unref();
}

/** One-line summary for the startup log. */
export function describeSettings() {
    const parts = [];

    }

### Connection protection (anti-DDoS and anti-VPN)

The dedicated multiplayer server rate-limits new connections and the messages
players send, and can refuse players whose address belongs to a VPN, proxy, or
hosting provider. Singleplayer is unaffected.

Anti-DDoS is on by default: 12 connection attempts per 10 seconds and 5
simultaneous sockets per address, 256 sockets server-wide, roughly 900 messages
in a burst and 300 per second per player, plus a 1-minute limit to log in. An
address that keeps tripping the limits is blocked for 10 minutes. A small
amount of burst is normal (chunk loading), so these values are far above real
play.

Anti-VPN is also on by default and looks each new address up once, caching the
answer for six hours. The default provider, [ip-api.com](https://ip-api.com),
needs no account (free, non-commercial, HTTP only). For more accurate results
and datacenter detection use [proxycheck.io](https://proxycheck.io) with a key:

```sh
SERVER_ANTIVPN_KEY=your-key SERVER_ANTIVPN_PROVIDER=proxycheck node server.js
```

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SERVER_ANTIDDOS` | `true` | Set to `false` to disable connection/message flood limits. |
| `SERVER_ANTIVPN` | `true` | Set to `false` to disable address reputation checks. |
| `SERVER_ANTIVPN_PROVIDER` | `ipapi` | `ipapi` or `proxycheck`. |
| `SERVER_ANTIVPN_KEY` | — | proxycheck.io key. Without it the server uses ip-api.com. |
| `SERVER_ANTIVPN_BLOCK_HOSTING` | `true` | Also refuse datacenter/hosting addresses. |
| `SERVER_ANTIVPN_FAIL_OPEN` | `true` | Allow players when the lookup service is unreachable. Set to `false` to refuse them instead. |
| `SERVER_ANTIVPN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `3000` | Lookup timeout. |
| `SERVER_TRUST_PROXY` | `false` | Read the client address from `X-Forwarded-For`. Enable only behind a reverse proxy you control, otherwise clients can spoof it. |

Refused players see a disconnect screen explaining why. Loopback and LAN
addresses are never looked up.

Added both protections to the dedicated server. Singleplayer is untouched: the integrated server passes no socket request, so its gate is `null` and nothing in the new module runs there.

**Anti-DDoS** — [security.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/security.js), wired into the upgrade in [server.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/server.js) via `verifyClient` and into the socket in [ServerRuntime.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/ServerRuntime.js#L117):
- 12 connection attempts per 10 s per address, at most 5 sockets open per address, 256 sockets server-wide. Refusals happen during the HTTP upgrade, so no WebSocket or game state is ever created.
- Per-socket message budget (~900 burst, 300/s) plus 1 MiB text / 4 MiB binary caps, and a 1-minute limit to get in game.
- Addresses that keep tripping limits are blocked for 10 minutes; already-open sockets from a blocked address are cut on their next message.
- If `X-Forwarded-For` is spoofable this would be bypassable, so it is only honoured with `SERVER_TRUST_PROXY=true`.

**Anti-VPN** — the same module, running per connection:
- Each public address is classified once and cached for 6 hours; loopback, LAN and CGNAT are never looked up.
- Default provider is ip-api.com (no account needed). `SERVER_ANTIVPN_PROVIDER=proxycheck` with `SERVER_ANTIVPN_KEY` gives better accuracy and datacenter typing.
- Datacenter/hosting ranges are blocked too by default (`SERVER_ANTIVPN_BLOCK_HOSTING=false` allows them).
- Lookups fail open by default so a provider outage can't lock everyone out (`SERVER_ANTIVPN_FAIL_OPEN=false` to fail closed, 3 s timeout).
- Messages that arrive before the verdict are buffered (up to 32) and replayed if the player is allowed; a blocked player gets a login disconnect screen naming the reason, e.g. *“Connections through a VPN or proxy are not allowed on this server.”*

Both can be disabled with `SERVER_ANTIDDOS=false` / `SERVER_ANTIVPN=false`. Everything is documented in [README.md](README.md) and as commented variables in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml).

Verified by booting the server and exercising the real paths: a loopback client connected and got its status reply; then 15 rapid connections produced 11 accepted and 4 refused with `connection flood (13 attempts in 10s)` logged; a `1.1.1.1` client (via trusted proxy header) received a 95-byte disconnect packet and was closed with `Refused 1.1.1.1: Connections through datacenter/hosting address…`; a residential address was allowed and both buffered messages were replayed. Direct module checks confirmed loopback/LAN skip lookup and that repeated lookups hit the cache. No test files were added.

Two limitations worth knowing: ip-api.com's free tier is HTTP-only and non-commercial, so for a public server proxycheck.io with a key is the sturdier choice; and an address flagged by the provider stays blocked for the 6-hour cache even if it changes hands sooner.

A natural next step is operator control over the blocklist, since right now a false positive is invisible in game.

+### Connection protection (anti-DDoS and anti-VPN)
+
+The dedicated multiplayer server rate-limits new connections and the messages
+players send, and can refuse players whose address belongs to a VPN, proxy, or
+hosting provider. Singleplayer is unaffected.

+simultaneous sockets per address, 256 sockets server-wide, roughly 900 messages
+in a burst and 300 per second per player, plus a 1-minute limit to log in. An
+address that keeps tripping the limits is blocked for 10 minutes. A small
+amount of burst is normal (chunk loading), so these values are far above real
+play.
+

+answer for six hours. The default provider, [ip-api.com](https://ip-api.com),
+needs no account (free, non-commercial, HTTP only). For more accurate results
+and datacenter detection use [proxycheck.io](https://proxycheck.io) with a key:

+// Connection hardening for the standalone multiplayer server.
+//
+// Two independent layers live here:
+//
+//   1. Anti-DDoS: refuse floods of new sockets from one address, cap the
+//      number of sockets an address may hold open, and rate-limit the messages
+//      an established socket can send. Repeat offenders are blocked for a
+//      while instead of being hammered on individually.
+//
+//   2. Anti-VPN: ask an IP-reputation service whether an address belongs to a
+//      VPN, proxy or hosting provider and refuse the login when it does.
+//      Results are cached (reputation changes slowly), lookups never block the
+//      event loop, and a service outage falls back to the configured
+//      fail-open/fail-closed behaviour.
+//

+// real socket request is available, so the singleplayer integrated server
+// (which runs inside a browser worker and is reached through a loopback
+// adapter) is never affected.

+import Logger from './logger.js';

+    if (['0', 'false', 'no', 'off'].includes(value)) return false;
+    if (['1', 'true', 'yes', 'on'].includes(value)) return true;
+    return fallback;
+}
+
+function envInt(name, fallback, min, max) {
+    const parsed = parseInt(ENV[name], 10);
+    if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;
+    return Math.max(min, Math.min(max, parsed));

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Settings
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+export const settings = {
+    antiDdos: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIDDOS', true),
+    antiVpn: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIVPN', true),
+    // "ipapi" needs no account (free, non-commercial, HTTP only). "proxycheck"
+    // is more accurate and adds datacenter detection, but needs a key.
+    vpnProvider: String(ENV.SERVER_ANTIVPN_PROVIDER || 'ipapi').trim().toLowerCase(),
+    vpnKey: String(ENV.SERVER_ANTIVPN_KEY || '').trim(),
+    // Datacenter/hosting ranges are blocked by default: a server owner who only
+    // wants to stop VPNs (and not, say, cloud-hosted friends) can turn this off.
+    blockHosting: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIVPN_BLOCK_HOSTING', true),
+    // Fail open keeps the server playable when the reputation service is down.
+    vpnFailOpen: envFlag('SERVER_ANTIVPN_FAIL_OPEN', true),
+    vpnTimeoutMs: envInt('SERVER_ANTIVPN_TIMEOUT_MS', 3000, 250, 15000),

Fixed for the proxied deployment. Because `play.breakmine.com` terminates the connection, every socket arrived at the game server with the proxy's address, which would have made the per-IP limits one shared bucket for the whole server (5 sockets total, 12 joins per 10 s) and given every player a single shared VPN verdict — usually "datacenter", i.e. everyone blocked.

The server now resolves the player's real address in [security.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/security.js#L156) before applying either protection:

- If the connecting peer is a **loopback or LAN** address (nginx, Caddy, cloudflared on the same box or network), forwarded headers are trusted automatically — no config needed for your setup.
- The address comes from `CF-Connecting-IP` first (Cloudflare always overwrites it), then the **last** `X-Forwarded-For` entry, which is the address your proxy actually saw rather than anything the client typed.
- A **public** peer's headers are ignored entirely, so a client cannot spoof its way past the limits or the VPN check by hitting the game port directly.
- If your proxy reaches the game container from a public address, name it: `SERVER_TRUST_PROXY=203.0.113.10`. `SERVER_TRUST_PROXY=true` trusts any peer and prints a warning in the startup log; `false` goes back to socket addresses only.

The startup line now tells you which mode is live, e.g. `anti-DDoS on (...); trusting forwarded client IPs from loopback/LAN proxies; anti-VPN on via ip-api.com, ...`.

Verified by running the real server with **no trust-proxy env** (the loopback-proxy case): a connection claiming `1.1.1.1` was refused with `Refused 1.1.1.1: Connections through a datacenter/hosting address are not allowed on this server.` and got its disconnect screen, while a residential address was allowed and received its buffered status reply. Header resolution was also checked directly across all modes — loopback peer + XFF, LAN peer + multi-hop XFF, `CF-Connecting-IP` precedence, spoofed XFF from a public peer (ignored), explicit proxy list, `false`, and `true`. No tests were added.

One thing to confirm on your side: the per-IP limits are only meaningful if players reach the game port *through* the proxy. If `6008` is also published straight to the internet (it is in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml)), those direct connections bypass the proxy — worth binding that port to localhost or firewalling it.

#
# cors.js on :6006. It answers the API on every hostname, and additionally
# serves the game client when the request is for the site hostname

# ---- asset generation stage --------------------------------------------------
FROM node:24-slim AS assets

WORKDIR /app

# src/resources.js (7 MB) and src/js/assetManifest.js are generated from the
# source tree by scripts/build-assets.js and are gitignored, so a fresh checkout
# cannot serve the client without this step. The script uses only node builtins,

COPY scripts/ ./scripts/
COPY src/ ./src/

// Assemble the static site directory that the Nixpacks deployment serves.
//
// The client is native ES modules with no bare imports, so it is served from
// source (no Vite build) exactly like the Docker image does. Vite is a
// devDependency and is not installed by a production `npm install`, which is
// why `serve dist` 404s on a fresh deploy: `dist/` is gitignored and nothing
// creates it.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const root = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
const outDir = path.join(root, 'public');
const DIRECTORIES = ['src', 'libraries', '.well-known'];
const FILES = ['index.html', 'style.css', 'loading.gif', 'catalog.json', 'openapi.json', 'api-docs.html', '_headers', 'CNAME'];

fs.rmSync(outDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });

let copied = 0;
for (const dir of DIRECTORIES) {
    const from = path.join(root, dir);
    if (!fs.existsSync(from)) { console.warn(`[site] skipping missing ${dir}/`); continue; }
    fs.cpSync(from, path.join(outDir, dir), { recursive: true });
    copied++;
}
for (const file of FILES) {
    const from = path.join(root, file);
    if (!fs.existsSync(from)) continue;
    fs.copyFileSync(from, path.join(outDir, file));
    copied++;
}

if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(outDir, 'index.html'))) {
    throw new Error('client entry point index.html is missing');
}
if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(outDir, 'src', 'resources.js'))) {
    console.warn('[site] src/resources.js is missing - run scripts/build-assets.js first');
}
console.log(`[site] Assembled ${outDir} (${copied} entries)`);

Fixed. To be clear about the cause: the 404 was not from the security work — those changes only run inside the game server process on `6008`. The site is served by `npx serve -s dist -l 3000` in [nixpacks.toml](nixpacks.toml), and `dist/` only exists after a Vite build. Vite is a devDependency, the Nixpacks install runs with `--omit=dev` (that `npm warn config production Use --omit=dev` line in your log), and `dist/` is gitignored — so a fresh build has no `dist/` at all and serve answers every request with 404. Your commit triggered a rebuild, which is why the previously served copy disappeared.

The deployment now serves the same source tree the Docker image already serves, instead of a build artifact that never exists:

- [scripts/build-site.js](scripts/build-site.js) assembles `public/` from `src/`, `libraries/`, `.well-known/`, `index.html`, `style.css`, `loading.gif` and the catalog/docs files.
- [nixpacks.toml](nixpacks.toml) runs it after `build-assets.js` and serves `public` instead of `dist`.
- `public/` is gitignored so the assembled tree never lands in a commit.

Verified by running the exact production commands locally (`build-assets.js`, then `build-site.js`, then `npx serve -s public -l 3101`): `/` returns the 71 KB `index.html` as `text/html`, `/style.css` `text/css`, `/loading.gif` `image/gif`, `/src/js/Start.js` and `/libraries/pako.es5.min.js` as `application/javascript`, a texture as `image/png`, and `/src/resources.js` (the generated 15 MB asset bundle) as `application/javascript`. All 200 with the content types the native-ESM client needs. `build-assets.js` also reports the expected asset summary, so the generated bundle is present before the copy.

These three changes are uncommitted, so the site stays broken until they're committed and the Nixpacks build runs again. Also worth knowing: serving the tree this way exposes only `public/`, not the repo root — the checkouts contain `data/`, `players/` and `serverconfig.conf`, which should never be reachable over HTTP.

+// Assemble the static site directory served by the Nixpacks deployment.
+//
+// The client is native ES modules with no bare npm imports, so it is served
+// straight from source, exactly like the Docker image serves /app/public.
+// There is deliberately no Vite build here: vite is a devDependency and a
+// production install omits it, so a fresh deploy has no dist/ to serve (it is
+// gitignored and nothing creates it). That is why `serve -s dist` answered
+// every request with a 404.
+const fs = require('fs');
+const path = require('path');
+
+const root = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
+const outDir = path.join(root, 'public');
+
+const DIRECTORIES = ['src', 'libraries', '.well-known'];
+const FILES = [
+    'index.html',
+    'style.css',
+    'loading.gif',
+    'catalog.json',
+    'openapi.json',
+    'api-docs.html',
+    '_headers',
+    'CNAME'
+];
+
+fs.rmSync(outDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
+fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
+
+let entries = 0;
+
+for (const dir of DIRECTORIES) {
+    const from = path.join(root, dir);
+    if (!fs.existsSync(from)) {
+        console.warn(`[site] Skipping missing ${dir}/`);
+        continue;
+    }
+    fs.cpSync(from, path.join(outDir, dir), { recursive: true });
+    entries++;
+}
+
+for (const file of FILES) {
+    const from = path.join(root, file);
+    if (!fs.existsSync(from)) continue;
+    fs.copyFileSync(from, path.join(outDir, file));
+    entries++;
+}
+
+if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(outDir, 'index.html'))) {
+    throw new Error('index.html is missing, nothing to serve');
+}
+if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(outDir, 'src', 'resources.js'))) {
+    console.warn('[site] src/resources.js is missing - run scripts/build-assets.js first');
+}
+
+console.log(`[site] Assembled ${outDir} (${entries} entries)`);

Progress note:
Fixed for the proxied deployment. Because `play.breakmine.com` terminates the connection, every socket arrived at the game server with the proxy's address, which would have made the per-IP limits one shared bucket for the whole server (5 sockets total, 12 joins per 10 s) and given every player a single shared VPN verdict — usually "datacenter", i.e. everyone blocked.

The server now resolves the player's real address in [security.js](src/js/net/minecraft/server/security.js#L156) before applying either protection:

- If the connecting peer is a **loopback or LAN** address (nginx, Caddy, cloudflared on the same box or network), forwarded headers are trusted automatically — no config needed for your setup.
- The address comes from `CF-Connecting-IP` first (Cloudflare always overwrites it), then the **last** `X-Forwarded-For` entry, which is the address your proxy actually saw rather than anything the client typed.
- A **public** peer's headers are ignored entirely, so a client cannot spoof its way past the limits or the VPN check by hitting the game port directly.
- If your proxy reaches the game container from a public address, name it: `SERVER_TRUST_PROXY=203.0.113.10`. `SERVER_TRUST_PROXY=true` trusts any peer and prints a warning in the startup log; `false` goes back to socket addresses only.

The startup line now tells you which mode is live, e.g. `anti-DDoS on (...); trusting forwarded client IPs from loopback/LAN proxies; anti-VPN on via ip-api.com, ...`.

Verified by running the real server with **no trust-proxy env** (the loopback-proxy case): a connection claiming `1.1.1.1` was refused with `Refused 1.1.1.1: Connections through a datacenter/hosting address are not allowed on this server.` and got its disconnect screen, while a residential address was allowed and received its buffered status reply. Header resolution was also checked directly across all modes — loopback peer + XFF, LAN peer + multi-hop XFF, `CF-Connecting-IP` precedence, spoofed XFF from a public peer (ignored), explicit proxy list, `false`, and `true`. No tests were added.

One thing to confirm on your side: the per-IP limits are only meaningful if players reach the game port *through* the proxy. If `6008` is also published straight to the internet (it is in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml)), those direct connections bypass the proxy — worth binding that port to localhost or firewalling it.

// Assemble the static site directory served by the Nixpacks deployment.
//
// The client is native ES modules with no bare npm imports, so it is served
// straight from source, exactly like the Docker image serves /app/public.
// There is deliberately no Vite build here: vite is a devDependency and a
// production install omits it, so a fresh deploy has no dist/ to serve (it is
// gitignored and nothing creates it). That is why `serve -s dist` answered
// every request with a 404.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const root = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
const outDir = path.join(root, 'public');

const DIRECTORIES = ['src', 'libraries', '.well-known'];
const FILES = [
    'index.html',
    'style.css',
    'loading.gif',
    'catalog.json',
    'openapi.json',
    'api-docs.html',
    '_headers',
    'CNAME'
];

fs.rmSync(outDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });

let entries = 0;

for (const dir of DIRECTORIES) {
    const from = path.join(root, dir);
    if (!fs.existsSync(from)) {
        console.warn(`[site] Skipping missing ${dir}/`);
        continue;
    }
    fs.cpSync(from, path.join(outDir, dir), { recursive: true });
    entries++;
}

for (const file of FILES) {
    const from = path.join(root, file);
    if (!fs.existsSync(from)) continue;
    fs.copyFileSync(from, path.join(outDir, file));
    entries++;
}

if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(outDir, 'index.html'))) {
    throw new Error('index.html is missing, nothing to serve');
}
if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(outDir, 'src', 'resources.js'))) {
    console.warn('[site] src/resources.js is missing - run scripts/build-assets.js first');
}

console.log(`[site] Assembled ${outDir} (${entries} entries)`);

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# cors.js on :6006. It answers the API on every hostname, and additionally
# serves the game client when the request is for the site hostname
# (SITE_HOSTNAMES, default breakmine.com), so one container can back both
# breakmine.com and api.breakmine.com. tunnel.js runs alongside it on :6007
# to relay WebSocket game traffic.

# ---- asset generation stage --------------------------------------------------
FROM node:24-slim AS assets

WORKDIR /app

# src/resources.js (7 MB) and src/js/assetManifest.js are generated from the
# source tree by scripts/build-assets.js and are gitignored, so a fresh checkout
# cannot serve the client without this step. The script uses only node builtins,
# so no npm install is needed here.
COPY scripts/ ./scripts/
COPY src/ ./src/
RUN node scripts/build-assets.js

# ---- runtime stage -----------------------------------------------------------
FROM node:24-slim

# better-sqlite3, bcrypt and discord-rpc have prebuilt binaries for linux, but
# fall back to compiling from source when none matches, so keep a toolchain.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        python3 make g++ ca-certificates \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    DATA_DIR=/data \
    PORT=6006 \
    TUNNEL_PORT=6007 \
    SITE_DIR=/app/public \
    SITE_HOSTNAMES=breakmine.com

WORKDIR /app

# package-lock.json is gitignored, so it is often missing from a fresh checkout
# and `npm ci` refuses to run without it. Prefer the lock when it is there.
COPY package*.json ./
RUN if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then \
        npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund; \
    else \
        npm install --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund; \
    fi \
    && npm cache clean --force

# --- the game client, served for SITE_HOSTNAMES ------------------------------
# No vite build: index.html is already a native-ESM entry point and the source
# tree has no bare npm imports, so the raw sources are servable as-is.
COPY --from=assets /app/src/ /app/public/src/
COPY index.html style.css /app/public/
COPY libraries/ /app/public/libraries/

# API discovery (RFC 9727). The catalog is copied in twice on purpose:
# .well-known/api-catalog is the well-known URI, catalog.json is the document
# itself, which the catalog may be served from per RFC 9727 s4. Both are read
# by cors.js from /app (not /app/public), so it gets its own copy below.
COPY .well-known/ /app/public/.well-known/
COPY catalog.json openapi.json api-docs.html /app/public/
COPY _headers /app/public/_headers

# --- the auth API -------------------------------------------------------------
COPY cors.js ./

# --- the WebSocket tunnel relay ----------------------------------------------
# tunnel.js relays game traffic over WS on TUNNEL_PORT. It needs only the `ws`
# package and node builtins, both already present.
COPY tunnel.js ./
# cors.js reads these from its own directory when serving the catalog,
# rel=service-desc and rel=service-doc.
COPY catalog.json openapi.json api-docs.html ./

# cors.js requires these two game modules directly:
#   src/js/net/minecraft/client/fs/IsomorphicFilesystem.js -> ./Filesystem.js, ../lib/pako.js
#   src/js/net/minecraft/server/logger.js
# Copy only those (~2 MB) instead of the whole 130 MB source tree.
COPY libraries/ ./libraries/
COPY src/js/net/minecraft/client/fs/ ./src/js/net/minecraft/client/fs/
COPY src/js/net/minecraft/lib/ ./src/js/net/minecraft/lib/
COPY src/js/net/minecraft/server/ ./src/js/net/minecraft/server/
COPY src/js/net/minecraft/util/ ./src/js/net/minecraft/util/
COPY src/js/net/minecraft/client/world/ ./src/js/net/minecraft/client/world/
COPY src/js/net/minecraft/client/command/ ./src/js/net/minecraft/client/command/
COPY server.js ./

# Named volume target. secrets.json is generated here on first boot, so it is
# never baked into the image; persisting /data keeps logins valid across rebuilds.
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown -R node:node /data /app
USER node

VOLUME ["/data"]
EXPOSE 6006 6007 6008

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:'+(process.env.PORT||6006)+'/',{headers:{host:process.env.SITE_HOSTNAMES?.split(',')[0]||'breakmine.com'}}).then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"

# Run the API and the tunnel relay together. `kill 0` forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT
# to the whole process group so both children shut down gracefully.
# If SERVER_PORT is set, run the multiplayer server instead.
CMD ["bash", "-c", "if [ -n \"$SERVER_PORT\" ]; then node /app/server.js; else trap 'kill 0' SIGTERM SIGINT; node cors.js & node tunnel.js & wait; fi"]

The deployed breakmine.com is a separate matter: it never runs Vite at all (`vite` isn't installed in a production deploy), it serves the static tree — which is why the old `serve -s dist` 404'd and why I added the copy.

Scaffolding is now a real multipart frame instead of one texture-mapped cube:

Each part is drawn with the block's own face textures (`["block", 326, box]`), so the plate shows `scaffolding_top` from above and `scaffolding_bottom` underneath, while the posts and plate edges show `scaffolding_side`. Because [renderFace](src/js/net/minecraft/client/render/BlockRenderer.js#L584-L620) derives UVs from a part's world-space size rather than stretching the whole texture, each part samples the slice of the texture it would have had in a full face — the posts pick up the frame's vertical border columns, the plate edges pick up the thick top band, so the parts line up as one continuous frame.

One thing had to change to make this safe: the world treats multipart parts as the block's collision shape (that's how fences and stairs work), which would have turned the frame into six solid boxes and killed both the walk-through and the climb.
